newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks jump in morning after Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks jump in morning after Wall St rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied strongly in Friday morning trade, as investors took direction from solid gains in U.S. stocks and bonds overnight.
The Hang Seng index was up 189.57 points at 13,036.13 after jumping to 13,107.46 in early trade. Turnover was HK$1.67 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"The market is following New York. The Dow Jones rose more than one hundred points overnight," said Teresa Wong, dealing director at DBS Securities.
The Dow industrials gained 126.87 points to 6,473.64 on Thursday, their second largest net gain ever. The U.S. long bond climbed 1-16/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said if the long bond yield continued to decline, Hong Kong stocks could push higher in the short term.
He said a lot of retail investors believed the market would stage a year-end rally. "Institutionally though it is pretty quiet," he added.
"I would have thought in terms of gains that at 13,100 it has done as much as it can do today. The market just gaps up and then goes sideways," Osborn said.
Interest rate sensitive property counters posted strong gains. Cheung Kong was up HK$1.00 at HK$65.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$1.50 to HK$93.50.
Henderson Land rose HK$1.25 to HK$73.00 and New World Development gained HK$0.70 at HK$47.90. New World Development is holding its annual general meeting on Friday.
In the banking sector, HSBC jumped HK$2.50 to HK$159.50 and Hang Seng Bank rose HK$1.25 to HK$91.00. Bank of East Asia added HK$0.30 to HK$33.20.
Despite the market's strong tone, shares of APT Satellite continued to decline. The stock shed HK$0.30 to HK$12.20 in early trade after dropping HK$1.00 on Thursday.
Dealing in the shares began on Wednesday when the stock closed at HK$13.50 compared with an issue price of HK$13.40.
